tools.search: Search this session's memory store for long-term memories (people, things, facts, events). Filter by keywords, entity (a name or e ID), type, and time range; with include_history, superseded or forgotten entries are returned too. Injected memories are only partial candidates: not finding something doesn't mean it didn't happen, so don't make things up. Someone appearing in a record only means they took part. The memory store is the authority on the past; if there's no record, say so plainly.
tools.noAccess: This session can't access that memory store
tools.factEvidence: Saving a fact or event needs content and evidence
tools.entityName: Saving an entity needs a name, or entity to name the entity to update

param.entityKind: Required when creating an entity (person or thing); may be omitted when only updating one
param.participants: Must be entities already in memory (a name, alias, or e ID); create people who appear in an event for the first time with kind=entity first
param.time: Absolute time: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM (without a time zone, the owner's time zone)

tools.get: Show the details of one memory: original evidence and source, what it replaced, and related conflicts; for an entity, its aliases, facts, and related events.
tools.forget: Forget a memory (archive it so it's no longer searched and won't be learned again automatically). Use only when the owner asks, or confirms it's wrong.
tools.resolve: Resolve a pending memory conflict (IDs start with c) according to the owner's answer. decision: keep:<ID> keeps one of them, both_valid means both hold, neither means neither holds, same_entity confirms they're the same person or thing and merges them, different_entity confirms they're different. owner_quote must be quoted exactly from the owner's answer this turn. If the owner only replied with a very short confirmation, owner_quote can be that word, quoted as is.
tools.save: Write or correct long-term memory. kind=entity creates or updates a person or thing (name, aliases, summary; merge combines duplicate entities); entity_kind is required when creating an entity (person/thing) and may be omitted when only updating one. kind=fact records a fact about an entity (states that change are fine, such as school year or job title). kind=event records something that happened or is planned; time must be absolute, converting words like "yesterday" using the date in the conversation, and if truly unsure, keep the original wording in time_text. Write content in the third person, without relative time words. participants must be entities already in memory (a name, alias, or e ID); create people who appear in an event for the first time with kind=entity before referring to them, or the write is rejected. evidence must be quoted exactly from this turn's owner message or a tool result; a quote from the owner's message counts as the owner's confirmation. Only record what the owner or the people involved explicitly said, never your own inferences. replaces corrects an existing entry.

log.summaryFailed: Short-term memory summary failed ({name}); retrying in 60 seconds
log.staleNames_one: {count} new name not seen for a long time
log.staleNames_other: {count} new names not seen for a long time
log.noEmbedding: Embedding unavailable; this {table} search uses keywords only

maintenance.questions_one: Memory has {count} question for the owner to confirm
maintenance.questions_other: Memory has {count} questions for the owner to confirm
maintenance.howTo: Ask the owner in passing in a message; after they answer, record it with memory_resolve

log.invalidEntry: Memory extraction dropped an invalid {key} entry
log.gateSkip: The decision model found nothing worth remembering ({hint:.2f}); skipping extraction
log.sessionFailed: Session memory extraction failed ({name}); retrying in {delay:.0f} s

conflict.maybeSame: may be {target} {name}; need to confirm whether they're the same

drop.assistant: The evidence is the assistant's own words
drop.notMember: The evidence isn't something a session member said
drop.relativeTime: The content is empty or contains relative time words
drop.forgotten: The owner asked to forget this before
drop.quoteMissing: The evidence quote isn't in the cited line
drop.future: A past event is dated after it was mentioned
drop.unknownId: Refers to an ID that doesn't exist: {value}
drop.unsupported: The decision model found the source doesn't support it, or it's an instruction to the assistant

log.migrated_one: Migrated {count} old memory into a fact
log.merged: Memory entity e{source} merged into e{target}
log.vectorsPaused: Memory vector computing paused: {exc}; retrying in {backoff:.0f} s
log.resolved: Memory conflict c{key} resolved by the owner's answer: {brief}

result.olderState: Recorded as the older state before f{id}
result.conflict: Recorded, but it conflicts with f{id} ({conflict}); the owner needs to confirm

render.conflicted: (conflicting; waiting for the owner to confirm)

longterm.ownerMerge: The owner can't be merged into another entity
longterm.relativeWords: Memory content can't contain relative time words (
longterm.useAbsolute: ); convert them to absolute dates before saving
longterm.ownerForget: The owner can't be forgotten; forget specific facts instead
longterm.summaryRelative: The summary can't contain relative time words; write absolute dates
longterm.useEntity: ); use the entity argument to say which one to update
longterm.evidenceAmbiguous: evidence matches several places in the source; quote a longer piece
longterm.ownerQuote: owner_quote must be quoted exactly from the owner's message this turn
longterm.evidenceShort: evidence is too short; quote the original text that supports this memory exactly
longterm.sharedNames: These names also belong to other entities, so lookups by name will ask for an ID:
longterm.forgottenBefore: This was asked to be forgotten; it can only be recorded again if the owner explicitly asks this turn
longterm.eventFuture: A past event can't be dated after now; use phase=planned for future plans
longterm.eventAuthority: v{id} comes from a more reliable source; only the owner's explicit correction this turn can replace it
longterm.entityKind: Creating an entity needs entity_kind: person or thing
longterm.eventTime: Events need time (an absolute time); if the time is truly unclear, keep the original description in time_text
longterm.partialNote: Memory may be incomplete; no record doesn't mean it didn't happen. Use memory_get to see the evidence when you need the original text.
longterm.keptInvalid: {kept} isn't among the entries of conflict c{key}: {entries}
longterm.refInvalid: Invalid memory ID: {brief} (like e7, f12, v31, c4)
longterm.evidenceRule: evidence must be quoted exactly from the owner's message or a tool result this turn (not reworded, not from other turns); your own words and inferences can't be evidence.
longterm.decisionInvalid: decision must be keep:<ID>, both_valid, neither, same_entity, or different_entity
longterm.entityUnknown: Memory has no person or thing called “{brief}”; create it first with memory_save(kind=entity), or name it with e<ID>

times.absolute: Times must be absolute: YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM (a time zone is allowed)

log.noResult: The decision model gave no {point} result; using the text model or rules instead
